categoryDescription: Multi-source - Spans drawn from two distinct independent sources

sourceDocuments.title: Impossibility of Distributed Consensus with One Faulty Process
sourceDocuments.text: Distributed consensus algorithms in asynchronous network environments must circumvent the Fischer-Lynch-Paterson impossibility theorem by adopting randomized tie-breakers or partial synchrony assumptions.

sourceDocuments.title: Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance in Replicated Systems
sourceDocuments.text: Byzantine fault tolerant protocols guarantee safety and liveness provided that fewer than one-third of participating nodes act maliciously or exhibit arbitrary failure modes.

studentDocument.title: Fault-Tolerant Distributed Consensus Foundations
studentDocument.text: Distributed consensus algorithms in asynchronous network environments must circumvent the Fischer-Lynch-Paterson impossibility theorem by adopting randomized tie-breakers or partial synchrony assumptions. Furthermore, Byzantine fault tolerant protocols guarantee safety and liveness provided that fewer than one-third of participating nodes act maliciously or exhibit arbitrary failure modes.
